snippet::array-coerce.description: You can use a combination of a ternary operator and `Array.isArray` to make sure a value, `undefined`, `null` or an array is always returned as an array.

snippet::array-difference.description: You can use a combination of `filter` and `includes` to calculate the difference between two arrays.

snippet::array-filled-with.description: You can use `new Array` with `Array.prototype.fill` to create an array filled with identical elements

snippet::array-flatten.description: You can use `Array.prototype.flat` with `Infinity` as an argument to fully flatten an array.

snippet::array-from-count.description: You can use `Array.from` to create an array of sequential integers

snippet::array-from-count-with-start.description: You can use `Array.from` to create an array of sequential integers starting from a specific integer
snippet::array-from-count-with-start.example: Array.from({ length: end - start }, (_, i) => i + start);

snippet::array-last.description: You can use `arr.at(-1)` if supported or `arr[arr.length - 1]` to get the last element of an array.

snippet::array-slice-exclude-last-n.description: You can get all but the last n elements using `array.slice`

snippet::array-union.description: You can use a combination of the spread operator and `Set` to create a union of two arrays.

snippet::array-unique.description: You can convert to and from a `Set` to remove duplicates from an array.

snippet::assert.description: You can use a simple function to assert a value or an expression.

snippet::async-each.description: You can use `Promise.all` with `Array.prototype.map` to do an async action with an array of items.

snippet::async-function-constructor.description: You can get the `AsyncFunction` using `async function`.

snippet::base64.description: Every modern runtime provides a way to convert byte array to and from base64.

snippet::base64-id.description: You can use `crypto.randomBytes` with `Buffer.prototype.toString` to generate a random base64 id

snippet::call-bind.description: Every modern runtime provides a way to bind to the `call` method of a function.

snippet::char-last.description: You can use `str.at(-1)` if supported or `str[str.length - 1]` to get the last character of a string.

snippet::comver-to-semver.description: You can use a ternary operator and string concatenation to add a trailing `.0`.

snippet::find-first-defined.description: You can use `Array.prototype.find` to find a first defined item.

snippet::for-own.description: You can use `Object.keys(obj).forEach` to iterate over the own enumerable properties of an object.

snippet::get-iterator.description: Every modern runtime provides a way to get the iterator function through the `Symbol.iterator` symbol.

snippet::has-ansi.description: You can use the `includes` method on the string to check if a specific ANSI byte is present.

snippet::has-argv.description: You can use the `includes` method on the `process.argv` array to check if a flag is present.

snippet::indent-string.description: You can indent every non-empty line with `String.prototype.replace`, or use `/^/gm` to also indent empty lines, matching the package's `includeEmptyLines` option.
snippet::indent-string.example:
const indentString = (string, count = 1, indent = ' ') =>
  string.replace(/^(?!\s*$)/gm, indent.repeat(count));

snippet::is-arraybuffer.description: You can use `instanceof ArrayBuffer`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(obj) === "[object ArrayBuffer]"`

snippet::is-async-function.description: You can use `typeof` and `Object.prototype.toString.call` to check if it's an async function
snippet::is-async-function.example: const isAsyncFunction = (obj) => typeof obj === "function" && Object.prototype.toString.call(obj) === "[object AsyncFunction]"

snippet::is-aws-lambda.description: You can check if the current environment is an AWS Lambda by checking if the `LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT` environment variables are set.

snippet::is-bigint.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a bigint.

snippet::is-boolean.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a boolean.

snippet::is-ci.description: Every major CI provider sets a `CI` environment variable that you can use to detect if you're running in a CI environment.

snippet::is-date.description: You can use `instanceof Date`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object Date]"`

snippet::is-deflate-buffer.description: You can check the first two bytes of a buffer to detect if it's compressed using deflate.

snippet::is-directory.description: You can call `isDirectory()` on the result of `stat` from `node:fs/promises`, or of `statSync` from `node:fs`, treating an `ENOENT` error as `false`.

snippet::is-dotfile.description: You can test whether a path ends in a dotfile such as `.gitignore` using a regular expression.

snippet::is-electron.description: You can detect Electron by checking the renderer process type, `process.versions.electron`, or the user agent.

snippet::is-equal.description: You can determine if two values are equal using regular equality checks.

snippet::is-even.description: You can use the modulo operator to check if a number is even.

snippet::is-function.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a function.

snippet::is-generator-function.description: You can use `typeof` and `Object.prototype.toString.call` to check if a value is a generator function
snippet::is-generator-function.example: const isGeneratorFunction = (obj) => typeof obj === "function" && Object.prototype.toString.call(obj) === "[object GeneratorFunction]"

snippet::is-gzip-buffer.description: You can check first three bytes of a buffer to detect if it is a gzip file.

snippet::is-identifier-name.description: You can test a string against the `ID_Start` and `ID_Continue` Unicode properties to check whether it is a valid identifier name, and so usable as an unquoted property.

snippet::is-in-ssh.description: You can check if the current environment is SSH by checking if the `SSH_CONNECTION` environment variable is set.

snippet::is-interactive.description: You can check if the current environment is interactive using `process.stdout.isTTY` and checking that it is not running in CI.

snippet::is-jpg-buffer.description: You can check the first three bytes of a buffer against the JPEG file signature to detect if it is a JPEG image.

snippet::is-map.description: You can use `instanceof Map` to check if a value is a `Map`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object Map]"`

snippet::is-negative.description: You can check if a number is less than 0 to determine if it's negative.

snippet::is-negative-zero.description: You can use `Object.is` to check if a value is negative zero.

snippet::is-nil.description: You can check if a value is `null` or `undefined` using loose equality with `null`.

snippet::is-npm.description: If the current environment is npm the `npm_config_user_agent` environment variable will be set and start with `"npm"`.

snippet::is-null.description: You can check if a value is `null` using regular equality checks.

snippet::is-number.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a number.

snippet::is-object.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is an object and `Object.getPrototypeOf` to ensure it's a plain object.
snippet::is-object.example: const isObject = (obj) => obj && typeof obj === "object" && (Object.getPrototypeOf(obj) === null || Object.getPrototypeOf(obj) === Object.prototype);

snippet::is-object-or-function.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is an object or a function.
snippet::is-object-or-function.example: const isObjectOrFunction = (v) => v !== null && (typeof v === "object" || typeof v === "function");

snippet::is-odd.description: You can use the modulo operator to check if a number is odd.

snippet::is-path-equal-cwd.description: You can check if a path equals the current working directory using `path.relative`.
snippet::is-path-equal-cwd.example:
import { relative } from 'node:path'

const isPathCwd = (p) => !relative(p, process.cwd())

snippet::is-png-buffer.description: You can check the first eight bytes of a buffer against the PNG file signature to detect if it is a PNG image.

snippet::is-posix-bracket.description: You can test for a POSIX bracket expression such as `[:alpha:]` using a regular expression.

snippet::is-primitve.description: You can check `typeof` of a value to determine if it's a primitive. Note that `typeof null` is `"object"` so you need to check for `null` separately.
snippet::is-primitve.example: const isPrimitive = (value) => value === null || (typeof value !== "function" && typeof value !== "object");

snippet::is-regexp.description: You can use `instanceof RegExp` to check if a value is a regular expression, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object RegExp]"`.

snippet::is-root-user.description: You can use `process.getuid?.()` to check if a user is a root user.

snippet::is-set.description: You can use `instanceof Set` to check if a value is a `Set`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object Set]"`

snippet::is-stream.description: `node:stream` provides `isReadable` and `isWritable` methods that can be used to check if a stream is readable or writable.
snippet::is-stream.example:
import { isReadable, isWritable } from 'node:stream';
const isStream = (stream) => isReadable(stream) || isWritable(stream);

snippet::is-string.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a string.

snippet::is-supported-regexp-flag.description: The `RegExp` constructor throws on an unsupported or invalid flag, so you can check support with a `try`/`catch`.

snippet::is-symbol.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is a symbol.

snippet::is-touch-device.description: You can check if the current device is a touch device by checking the `'ontouchstart'` propery of the `window` object and `maxTouchPoints` of the `navigator` object.
snippet::is-touch-device.example: const isTouchDevice = window && ('ontouchstart' in window || navigator.maxTouchPoints)

snippet::is-travis.description: You can check if the current environment is Travis CI by checking if the `TRAVIS` environment variable is set.

snippet::is-typed-array.description: You can check if a value is a Typed Array using `ArrayBuffer.isView` and checking if it is not a `DataView`.

snippet::is-unc-path.description: You can test for a Windows UNC path such as `\\server\share` using a regular expression.

snippet::is-undefined.description: You can use `typeof` to check if a value is `undefined`.

snippet::is-upper-case.description: You can check if a string is upper case by comparing it to its upper case version.

snippet::is-weakmap.description: You can use `instanceof WeakMap` to check if a value is a `WeakMap`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object WeakMap]"`

snippet::is-weakset.description: You can use `instanceof WeakSet` to check if a value is a `WeakSet`, or if cross-realm, use `Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === "[object WeakSet]"`

snippet::is-whitespace.description: You can check if a string contains only whitespace with `RegExp` or by trimming it and comparing it to an empty string.

snippet::is-windows.description: You can check if the current environment is Windows by checking if `process.platform` is equal to "win32".

snippet::is-word-character.description: You can check if a character is a word character with a `RegExp`.

snippet::is-wsl.description: You can check if the current environment is WSL by checking if the `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` environment variable is set.

snippet::json-file.description: You can use `JSON` and `node:fs` to read and write JSON files.
snippet::json-file.example:
import * as fs from 'node:fs/promises'
fs.readFile(file, 'utf8').then(JSON.parse)
fs.writeFile(file, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n')

snippet::math-random.description: You can use `Math.random()` or `crypto.getRandomValues` if cryptographic randomness is required.

snippet::min-indent.description: You can use a regular expression with `Array.prototype.reduce` to find the shortest leading whitespace across the lines of a string.
snippet::min-indent.example: const minIndent = (string) => (string.match(/^[ \t]*(?=\S)/gm) ?? ['']).reduce((r, a) => Math.min(r, a.length), Infinity)

snippet::noop.description: You can use an arrow function `() => {}` for a noop function.

snippet::object-exclude.description: You can use `Object.fromEntries` with `Object.entries` and `Array.prototype.filter` to exclude specific keys from an object.

snippet::object-filter.description: You can use `Object.fromEntries` with `Object.entries` and `Array.prototype.filter` to filter an object's properties.

snippet::object-invert-key-value.description: You can use `Object.fromEntries` with `Object.entries` to invert keys and values.

snippet::object-iterate.description: You can use a `for...of` loop over `Object.entries` to iterate an object's own enumerable properties, and `break` to stop early.

snippet::object-map.description: You can use `Object.fromEntries` with `Object.entries` and `Array.prototype.map` to map an object's properties.
snippet::object-map.example: const objectMap = (obj, fn) => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(obj).map(([k, v]) => fn(k, v)));

snippet::object-reduce.example: const objectReduce = (obj, fn, initial) => Object.entries(obj).reduce((acc, [k, v]) => fn(acc, k, v), initial);

snippet::path-key.description: You can use `Object.keys` with `Array.prototype.findLast` to find the case-insensitive `PATH` environment variable key.

snippet::path-root.description: You can use `parse` from `node:path` and read its `root` property to get the root of a path.
snippet::path-root.example:
import { parse } from 'node:path'

const pathRoot = (filepath) => parse(filepath).root

snippet::regexp-copy.description: You can create a copy of a regular expression using the `RegExp` constructor.

snippet::set-function-length.description: You can set `length` of a function using `Object.defineProperty`.
snippet::set-function-length.example: const setFunctionLength = (fn, length) => Object.defineProperty(fn, 'length', { value: length, configurable: true });

snippet::set-function-name.description: You can set `name` of a function using `Object.defineProperty`.
snippet::set-function-name.example: const setFunctionName = (fn, name) => Object.defineProperty(fn, 'name', { value: name, configurable: true });

snippet::set-tostringtag.description: You can set the `toStringTag` of an object using `Object.defineProperty`.
snippet::set-tostringtag.example: const setToStringTag = (target, value) => Object.defineProperty(target, Symbol.toStringTag, { value, configurable: true });

snippet::split-lines.description: You can split a string into lines using a regular expression.

snippet::strip-bom.description: You can check if the first character of the string is the BOM and strip it using `String.prototype.slice` if it is.

snippet::trim-repeated-characters.description: You can trim repeated sequences of characters using `String.prototype.replace`.

snippet::typed-array-to-buffer.description: You can use `Buffer.from` to convert a Typed Array to `Buffer` and `ArrayBuffer.isView` to avoid a copy.

snippet::typeof.description: You can use `typeof` to get the type of a value, or `Object.prototype.toString.call` to get the internal [[Class]] of an object.

snippet::unix-paths.description: You can check the start of a path for the Windows extended-length path prefix and if it's not present, replace backslashes with forward slashes.

snippet::uppercase-first-character.description: You can uppercase the first character.

snippet::year.description: You can use `new Date().getUTCFullYear()` to get the current year.
